text.headline: Timeline of Bangladesh
text.text: Major events in the history of Bangladesh.

events.headline: Earliest Settlements
events.text: The earliest evidence of human settlements in the Bengal region dates back to around 2500 BCE, with archaeological findings indicating agricultural and urban development.

events.headline: Formation of the Kingdom of Bengal
events.text: The Kingdom of Bengal was established, marking the beginning of a distinct political entity in the region that would flourish for centuries.

events.headline: Muslim Conquest of Bengal
events.text: Bengal was conquered by Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khilji, leading to the establishment of Muslim rule in the region.

events.headline: Bengal Subah Established
events.text: The Mughal Empire established Bengal as a province, which became one of the richest and most important regions in the empire.

events.headline: Battle of Plassey
events.text: The British East India Company defeated the Nawab of Bengal, marking the beginning of British colonial rule in the region.

events.headline: Sepoy Mutiny
events.text: The Indian Rebellion of 1857, also known as the Sepoy Mutiny, had significant repercussions in Bengal, leading to direct British rule.

events.headline: Partition of India
events.text: British India was partitioned into India and Pakistan, with Bengal divided into West Bengal (India) and East Bengal (Pakistan).

events.headline: Language Movement
events.text: The Language Movement began in East Pakistan, advocating for the recognition of Bengali as an official language, which led to significant political activism.

events.headline: Bangladesh Liberation War
events.text: The Liberation War began with a declaration of independence from Pakistan, leading to a nine-month-long conflict.

events.headline: Independence of Bangladesh
events.text: Bangladesh achieved independence from Pakistan, officially becoming a sovereign nation.

events.headline: Assassination of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman
events.text: The founding leader of Bangladesh, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, was assassinated along with most of his family, leading to political turmoil.

events.headline: Fall of Military Rule
events.text: The military regime in Bangladesh ended following widespread protests, leading to the restoration of democracy.

events.headline: BNP Wins Elections
events.text: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) won the general elections, marking a significant political shift in the country.

events.headline: Awami League Returns to Power
events.text: The Awami League, led by Sheikh Hasina, won a landslide victory in the national elections, returning to power after two years of military-backed rule.

events.headline: Shahbagh Movement
events.text: The Shahbagh Movement emerged, demanding capital punishment for war criminals from the 1971 Liberation War, highlighting issues of justice and accountability.

events.headline: Controversial Elections
events.text: The general elections were held amid allegations of vote rigging and violence, resulting in the Awami League winning a third consecutive term.

events.headline: COVID-19 Pandemic
events.text: The COVID-19 pandemic reached Bangladesh, leading to nationwide lockdowns and significant impacts on health and the economy.

events.headline: 50th Anniversary of Independence
events.text: Bangladesh celebrated the 50th anniversary of its independence with various events and reflections on its journey since 1971.

events.headline: Ongoing Political Challenges
events.text: Bangladesh continues to face political challenges, including calls for democratic reforms and concerns over human rights.
